hints: Look carefully at list 1 to 5 and ask yourself which cells are prokaryotic and which have lost their nucleus, as both clues rule out mitosis.
Remember mitosis is nuclear division in eukaryotic cells with a nucleus, so think about why bacteria use binary fission and why a cell with no nucleus cannot start mitosis.
walkthrough:
**Recall what mitosis needs**

Great start. Mitosis is division of a eukaryotic nucleus to make two genetically identical nuclei. So a cell must be eukaryotic and must still have its nucleus and DNA to do it.

**Rule out 1 and 4**

Now check the odd ones out. 1 bacterial cells are prokaryotes with no true nucleus, so they divide by binary fission, not mitosis. 4 mature red blood cells in mammals have lost their nucleus, so they have no DNA to copy and cannot divide at all.

**Confirm 2, 3 and 5**

Now look at the rest. 2 cancer cells are eukaryotic animal cells that divide by mitosis very rapidly and uncontrollably. 3 lymphocytes divide by mitosis during clonal expansion in an immune response. 5 stem cells divide by mitosis for growth, repair and to produce specialised cells. That leaves 2, 3 and 5.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes 1 and 4. Bacteria divide by binary fission, and mature red blood cells have no nucleus so cannot divide.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes 1. Bacterial cells are prokaryotic and do not carry out mitosis, even though 2 and 3 do.
options.C: Correct. Cancer cells, lymphocytes and stem cells are all nucleated eukaryotic cells that can divide by mitosis.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes 4. Mature red blood cells lack a nucleus and cannot divide, even though 3 and 5 can.
